angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 542,646 km at 114.66 pc = 0.06 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 8.7212 +/- 0.0116 mas (same row, RUWE 0.80): 114.66 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.78 +/- 0.05 solar radii from Gomez Barrientos et al. 2025, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-1346 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025AJ....170..148G/abstract): 542,646 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.82 +/- 0.1 solar masses from Gomez Barrientos et al. 2025, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-1346 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025AJ....170..148G/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5099 +/- 50 K from Gomez Barrientos et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1346 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025AJ....170..148G/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Gomez Barrientos et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1346 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025AJ....170..148G/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-1346.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.568, rounded to two decimals

luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-1346 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -0.47288, from TICv8 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019AJ....158..138S/abstract)
